Who each one is for

Decide by what happens after the show.

Everything during the show is the same: four cameras, a button each, streaming without a computer. The ISO earns its price later.

ATEM Mini Pro · $349.00

  • A weekly meeting recorded as one file for the archive.

ATEM Mini Pro vs ISO questions.

Recording, 4K, streaming and which one for a church.

What is the difference between the ATEM Mini Pro and the ATEM Mini Pro ISO?

Both switch four HDMI cameras, stream over Ethernet and record the program. The ISO also records each of the four inputs as its own file, records audio as WAV files, and saves your cuts as a DaVinci Resolve project so the show can be re-edited.

Is the ISO worth the extra $236.00?

If anyone edits the recording afterwards, usually yes: the edit can cut to any camera at any moment, not only the one that was live. If the program is only streamed and archived as it was, the ATEM Mini Pro does the same job.

Do they record in 4K?

No. Both take HD inputs up to 1080p60 and output up to 1080p60; Blackmagic lists no Ultra HD formats for either.

Do they need a computer to stream?

No. Both stream directly over Ethernet using RTMP or SRT. A computer is only needed to set them up with the ATEM software, or as a slides source.

Which one should a church buy?

A church that streams the service as it happens can start with the ATEM Mini Pro, as in i9’s one-operator setup. A church that edits the sermon for social media afterwards gets more from the ISO.
